who: Tore C. Olsson, historian of modern US and agrarian history at Tennessee, PhD history Georgia 2013.

evidence.says: CV names Tore C. Olsson, lists Tennessee history appointments from 2013, and a Georgia history PhD in May 2013.
Authority identifies Olsson, Tore C.; its source is the 2017 prepublication title Remaking the rural world.
The Tore Olsson (2013) profile identifies the Tennessee historian and his first book as Remaking the Rural World: The American South and Mexico in the Twentieth Century.

notes: Full name, institution, doctorate and prepublication book title connect the candidate to the supervisor.

who: J. Gregory (Joseph Gregory) Oswald, historian of Soviet affairs at the University of Arizona.

evidence.says: Authority explicitly equates Joseph Gregory Oswald with the usage J. Gregory Oswald and cites The Krueger memoir (1993).
News of the Profession reports J. Gregory Oswald promoted to associate professor of history at the University of Arizona.
Contemporary Soviet Research on Latin America identifies its author as J. Gregory Oswald, University of Arizona.

notes: Distinctive authorized name and Arizona history affiliation support the match. The Stanford 1958 doctorate and specific 1981 supervision were not independently verified.

who: Hyland Bryant Packard, historian of recent America at the University of Houston, PhD LSU.

evidence.says: University of Houston Faculty Vita Records contain a folder for Packard, Hyland B., in the 1960–1990 collection.
Identifies Hyland Bryant Packard as a retired University of Houston professor of recent American history and names his LSU dissertation, Critic as Witness: Francis Hackett and His America, 1883–1914.
Candidate authority is Packard, H. Jeremy, citing The battle cry of freedom (1983), without education or institutional affiliation.

notes: The supervisor is identifiable, but no source connects Hyland Bryant Packard to H. Jeremy Packard. Different fuller names raise doubt; the sparse candidate record does not establish a definitive exclusion.

who: Leroy E. Page, historian of science at Kansas State University.

evidence.says: The Leroy E. Page fund description identifies Professor Page as the department historian of science for a quarter century.
A 1994 article on Kansas geological surveys identifies author Leroy E. Page with Kansas State University’s Department of History.
Closest candidate is authorized as Page, Leroy W., citing California gold book (1977), with no career or degree information.
Another candidate is identified as Lionel Frank Page, associated with Wisdom from Nonsense Land.
The remaining candidate is Luke Flood Page, a clergyman and author of Two sermons (1845).

notes: Lionel and Luke Flood Page are different people. The closest candidate has a conflicting middle initial and no institutional evidence; a match to Leroy W. Page remains unproven.

who: Paula F. Pfeffer, historian of modern American social reform and labor at Loyola Chicago, PhD Northwestern 1980.
